response = "The general discipline is therefore to separate resource variability from protection and inertia performance by time scale and by mechanism. Variability in wind and solar output unfolds over minutes and is covered by reserve and dispatch arrangements, whereas protection misoperation, ride-through settings and inertia shortfalls express themselves in milliseconds to seconds, where they appear directly in fault records and frequency traces. Operators then compare measured plant behaviour against the registered performance standards, and run dynamic simulations in which settings, protection schemes and load shedding timings are varied to see which deficiencies, if corrected, would have preserved supply. A sudden regional fall in wind speed reduced wind farm output immediately before the first transmission fault. The final report concluded that the blackout was not caused by the intermittency of wind generation; a collapse of the wind resource ahead of the initiating fault and a verdict exonerating intermittency cannot both be true. The rate of change of frequency after the interconnector separation exceeded 6 Hz per second, and as a result the available under-frequency load shedding scheme could not operate quickly enough to arrest the frequency decline. The market operator measured the rate of change of frequency at 0.5 Hz per second following separation, a value that cannot be squared with the far steeper decline the event recordings establish. The islanded system carried insufficient synchronous inertia to survive the loss of the interconnector, and it was precisely that inertia deficit which drove the frequency down so steeply. Tornadoes damaged transmission towers on two 275 kV lines north of Adelaide, and that structural damage caused six voltage dips to be recorded on the South Australian transmission network within about 87 seconds. The wind turbine voltage ride-through settings limited the number of voltage disturbances the turbines would tolerate before reducing output, and because that tolerance was exhausted, nine wind farms reduced their combined output by 456 MW during the voltage disturbances. The sudden withdrawal of those 456 MW in turn caused the Heywood interconnector to trip, well after the towers north of Adelaide had come down. The Heywood interconnector remained in service throughout the event: either the link separated from the eastern system or it carried power without interruption for the whole duration, one of the two and never both. Attribution in an event of this kind begins with who holds the inquiry and what evidence it can reach. The Australian Energy Market Operator was responsible for investigating the 28 September 2016 South Australian system black event. Investigators reconstructed the sequence of the event using time-synchronised data from phasor measurement units, fault recorders and SCADA logs, which is what allows a sub-second ordering of faults, control actions and generator responses."
